verified_claims: The Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model covering about 99 percent of England.
The DTM removes buildings, vegetation and other surface objects to model terrain surface.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, newer and better-resolution source data is preferred.
Resampled source data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
The published composite includes surveys spanning multiple years, so survey-age metadata is location dependent.
Metadata survey-index catalogues identify the survey used for a location.
WCS is the supported open-standard service for retrieving raw elevation pixels.
WMS provides a summarised visual representation and must not be substituted for numeric WCS values.
WCS services use OGC version 2.0.1 endpoints.
Stable service names replaced release-year-suffixed image-service endpoints.
Time-stamped DTM tiles are distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km archives.
LIDAR elevations are supplied in metres and aligned to the OS National Grid.
Vertical values are referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The Composite is transformed using the OSTN15 geoid model.
Individual surveys used in composites report approximately plus or minus 15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
DTM and DSM have different surface semantics and must not be interchanged.
Interpolation and survey age must be retained in candidate-level provenance.
A generic product accuracy statement is not a candidate-specific uncertainty calculation.
No exact TQ2892 WCS coverage bytes or candidate pixel values were retrieved in this wave.
No candidate-specific authoritative height difference can be promoted without exact coverage and pixel readback.
